gitCommit.subject: fix: clear the four open bugs (a11y live regions, /file existence oracle, e2e flake, screenshot drain) (#316)
gitCommit.body:
fix: clear the four open bugs (a11y live regions, /file existence oracle, e2e flake, screenshot drain) (#316)

* fix(a11y): announce upload errors and status to screen readers (purses-orsx)

PhotoUpload rendered its failure message as plain text in a Card and
PoolUpload's per-file status list had no live region, so both were silent
to AT users (WCAG 2.1 AA, SC 4.1.3 Status Messages).

- PhotoUpload: the error Card is now role="alert" — a single blocking
  failure should interrupt.
- PoolUpload: the status list is role="status" aria-live="polite" — the
  region is mounted for the whole run so per-file transitions announce in
  place, and a batch never interrupts once per file.

Flips the two assertions that PINNED the gap into assertions that demand
the live regions.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Tb3s1QSGtkTEuF18Euaqf6

* fix(security): close /file existence oracle — authz before existence (purses-ct0)

Both photo /file routes resolved the item/photo (404) BEFORE the capability
gate (403), letting an authenticated non-member distinguish "this photo is
in that collection" from "it isn't".

Both routes already know the collectionId from the URL, so they never need
to resolve the item to decide access: hoist requireApiCapability above the
existence checks. A stranger now gets an identical 403 either way (and two
fewer DB round-trips on the reject path).

Fixes the pool /file route too — the bead named only the item route, but its
sibling had the identical ordering.

Also clears mockBlobGet per test: the "never serves bytes" assertions were
reading calls accumulated from the earlier 200-status tests and passed only
by accident of declaration order.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Tb3s1QSGtkTEuF18Euaqf6

* fix(e2e): deflake compare navigation — settle the round-end refresh (purses-pw52)

sort-session.spec raced the compare goto against the round-end router.refresh():
awaiting the RSC response proves the NETWORK settled, not that the client router
did, so a competing navigation to /triage could abort the in-flight goto
("interrupted by another navigation"). CI-only; always cleared on retry.

Retry the goto inside expect().toPass(). This absorbs the transient interruption
without masking a regression — the compare heading is still asserted inside the
retry, so a gate that genuinely kept redirecting to /triage would exhaust the
retries and fail.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Tb3s1QSGtkTEuF18Euaqf6

* fix(screenshots): per-theme usage queue so the dark run isn't drained (purses-z23h)

capture light and capture dark share one seeded DB serially. The usage-round
recap block answers every queued item, draining the queue — so the dark run
found an empty queue and timed out at usage-round-quick ("Quick pace" absent).

Seed a journey scenario PER THEME instead of sharing one. Chose this over
"skip gracefully when drained": skipping would leave dark silently producing NO
usage-round screenshots, which is the whole point of the capture (and is exactly
why the workaround was to run dark alone).

Verified: one `npm run screenshots` run now captures both themes — 29 light /
29 dark, with usage-round-quick-dark rendering the full round.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Tb3s1QSGtkTEuF18Euaqf6

* docs: sync API.md for the /file authz reorder + refresh graph (purses-ct0)

Both photo /file route entries asserted "belongs-to-parent (404) + member/owner
(403)" — the ordering this branch inverted. Correct them, and record the closed
existence oracle in Known authz gaps (incl. why the same reorder is NOT available
to requireApiItemCapability, which is the separate purses-3al surface).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Tb3s1QSGtkTEuF18Euaqf6

* fix(security): close the oracle on the WRITE verbs too, not just /file (purses-ct0)

Adversarial review (Security persona) caught that fixing GET /file alone was
theater: the identical bit was still readable by sending PATCH to the same
photoId. Every collection-scoped item/photo route resolved existence (404)
before the capability gate (403).

Hoist requireApiCapability above the existence checks on the rest of the surface:
  …/items/[itemId]/photos/[photoId]      PATCH, DELETE
  …/items/[itemId]/photos/[photoId]/set-hero  POST
  …/items/[itemId]/photos                POST
  …/items/[itemId]                       PATCH
A scan of every collection-scoped handler now reports no existence-before-authz.

Tests: the oracle test covers the write verbs, and is revert-detecting (reverting
the reorder yields "PATCH photo (rotate): real vs nonexistent must be
indistinguishable: expected 404 to be 403"). Also clears mockBlobGet in
pool-routes.integration.test.ts — its "never serves bytes" assertions had the same
declaration-order bug fixed here earlier.

Docs: API.md claimed the oracle was closed while PATCH still leaked it, and cited
purses-3al as the tracker for the residual items/** surface — but that bead is
CLOSED and was a different class (requireAuth-only IDOR). Both corrected, and the
two oracles this does NOT close (collection existence, top-level /api/items/**)
are now stated plainly instead of implied.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Tb3s1QSGtkTEuF18Euaqf6

* fix(a11y): rebuild the pool live region — it announced too much, then nothing (purses-orsx)

Adversarial review (UX + QA + Craftsman all converged) showed my first fix was
wrong in both directions, and its comment asserted the opposite of the platform:

- role="status" carries implicit aria-atomic="true", so <ul role="status"> re-read
  ALL N rows on every one of ~3N transitions — a 20-photo batch (a blessed flow per
  PRODUCT.md) became a torrent, not a status message.
- It also overrode the list role, so the per-file results were no longer browsable
  as a list.
- And on the drop-only-unsupported-files path the region mounted WITH its content and
  never mutated again — announcing nothing at all. That is the exact SC 4.1.3 failure
  the bead exists to fix, shipped inside the fix.

Rebuild: the <ul> goes back to a plain list, and a PERSISTENTLY-mounted sr-only
role="status" carries one coarse, rewritten sentence ("3 photos added, 1 photo
couldn't be added."). Atomic is right for one sentence; mounted-before-content is
what makes a live region actually announce.

Also: the raw thrown message ("Vercel Blob: Failed to retrieve the client token") was
being SPOKEN — map it to a person-side sentence (TONE), keep the raw for the console.
PhotoUpload: key the alert on a nonce so a REPEATED identical rejection re-announces
(setError(null)+setError(msg) batch into one commit, so the alert never re-fired).

Tests now pin behavior, not attributes — and both are revert-detecting:
  - the live region exists and is EMPTY before any file is picked (fails on the old
    conditionally-mounted design)
  - the skipped-only path announces rather than going silent
  - a repeated identical rejection replaces the alert NODE (asserting text alone
    would pass with the bug present)

e2e: tighten the compare-goto retry (30s→10s/3s) so a latency regression fails fast
instead of being absorbed; the product-side race is filed as purses-hzwj.
screenshots: seed the journey PER TEST rather than a beforeAll Record — simpler, and
retry-safe (beforeAll does not re-run on a Playwright retry, so a retried dark attempt
would have re-consumed the drained queue).

Follow-ups filed: purses-hzwj (product race), purses-l5gd (success/progress still not
announced — SC 4.1.3 covers success), purses-r4it (capture.ts has no CI guard).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Tb3s1QSGtkTEuF18Euaqf6

* chore: refresh knowledge graph after review remediation

Node count drops by 2 — the capture.ts THEMES/Theme/triageSeeds symbols were
removed in favour of a per-test seed, so --force is expected here.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Tb3s1QSGtkTEuF18Euaqf6

webServer.command: npm run build && npx next start --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 3100

specs.title: authenticate
a11y: core authed screens — no serious/critical violations (light)
a11y: core authed screens — no serious/critical violations (dark)
a11y: unauthenticated login/signup — no serious/critical violations (light)
a11y: unauthenticated login/signup — no serious/critical violations (dark)
pool-first: Make items routes to the pool
both: Photo pool renders before Items, with the item preview shown
items-first: View all items routes to the items grid
empty: offers exactly one add-photos action and no pool/items sections
keyboard traversal reaches header → primary section → secondary actions → owner utilities in order
UI login redirects to /collections and the session survives middleware
after UI login, direct navigation to a protected route stays authenticated
login with bad credentials establishes no session and shows an error
login with good credentials signs in as that user
signup creates a fresh account and signs in as that user

suites.title: compare — which do you love more?

specs.title: renders the prompt, two choice cards, and quiet Tie/Skip escapes
tapping a card chooses it and the next pair (or a graceful end) appears
gentle progress text appears after a comparison is made
crash-reload: the gate drains pending decisions in queue order BEFORE the round re-renders
pagehide: a still-pending decision is delivered on unload and persists
owner types the name to permanently delete, then lands on /collections

suites.title: delete photo from the item carousel

specs.title: deleting the only photo (real DELETE) returns the add-photos CTA
the items grid requests the resized card width (w=640)
the item-detail hero requests the large width (w=1280)
